title: Calibrating Atlantis model with atlantio and calibrar
text: described Morell et al. (2026), goal using calibrar automate running batches simulations improve model fit, letting modellers nudge model right direction. model run many times, set parameters shuffle optionally revisited calibration progresses. Atlantis model includes tremendous number parameters, calibrating reach. Instead, calibration proceeds rounds: small set parameters chosen (e.g. growth clearance rates groups), optimizer calibrar (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=calibrar) searches values, results inspected, set parameters bounds revised next round. round involves steps: choosing parameters calibrate, bounds scale; assembling model inputs way run model; designing objective function runs model candidate parameter set returns score; running optimization, usually parallel; inspecting results, including runs crashed. atlantio handles Atlantis-specific parts: checking input files, reading writing parameter files, expanding calibration table, transforming parameter values, reading model output scoring . calibrar handles optimization. Morell et al. (2026) use atlantis2ls (https://github.com/alaiam/atlantis2ls) role atlantio.

title: Calibrating Atlantis model with atlantio and calibrar
text: See https://roliveros-ramos.github.io/calibrar/articles/calibrar.html. calibrar::calibrate() minimizes objective function fn(par, ...) parameter vector par bounded lower upper. evolutionary strategy method = "AHR-ES", every generation evaluates population popsize parameter sets; parallel = TRUE, evaluations spread workers registered foreach backend. state optimization saved restart file every REPORT generations, interrupted calibration resumes stopped. Everything therefore boils writing one R function takes parameter vector, writes corresponding Atlantis input files, runs model, reads output returns single number. rest vignette walks building function running calibrar.

text: objective function chains one calibration iteration: apply parameters: apply_parameters() maps values calibration scale model scale sets parameter files loaded model object; create unique run directory write inputs write_parameter_folder(): copies base inputs writes biology file calibrated values changed, keeping comments units; add run script; run model check, check_run(), completed; read output compute score; save time series parameter values score, remove bulky run files. code: run_model <- function(par, atlantis, calib_table, base_dir, results_dir,                       groups) {   # the names <name>.<position> make every parameters.rds self-describing,   # and are what read_calibration_runs() expects   names(par) <- paste(calib_table$name, calib_table$position, sep = ".")    # 1. parameter values, on the model scale in the biology file   atlantis <- apply_parameters(atlantis, calib_table, par)   par_model <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(calib_table)), function(i) {     atlantis@biology[[calib_table$name[i]]][calib_table$position[i]]   }, numeric(1))   names(par_model) <- names(par)    # 2. run directory and input files   run_dir <- tempfile("run_", tmpdir = results_dir)   dir.create(run_dir)   write_parameter_folder(atlantis, run_dir, from = base_dir, overwrite = TRUE)   write_run_script(run_dir, init = "init.nc", run = "run.prm",     force = "force.prm", physics = "physics.prm", biology = "biology.prm",     groups = "groups.csv", fisheries = "fisheries.csv")    # 3. model run; a zero exit status does not mean the run completed   res <- run_atlantis(run_dir, timeout = 86400)   out_file <- file.path(run_dir, "outputFolder", "output.nc")   if (!res$complete) {     reason <- if (nrow(res$check)) res$check$message[1] else       if (res$timeout) "time limit reached" else       sprintf("exit status %s", res$status)     return(failed_run(run_dir, par, par_model, res, reason))   }    # 4. output and score; an error makes the run a failed one   out <- NULL   score <- tryCatch({     out <- atlantis_load_files(atlantis, out_file)     ts <- create_time_series_biomass(out, group = groups, aggregate = TRUE)     biomass <- read_biomass_index(       file.path(run_dir, "outputFolder", "outputBiomIndx.txt"),       atlantis@group     )     saveRDS(list(ts = ts, biomass = biomass),       file.path(run_dir, "time_series.rds"))     compute_score(ts, biomass = biomass)   }, error = function(e) e)   # the output is read through an open file handle: close it   if (!is.null(out)) try(ncdf4::nc_close(out@main_output), silent = TRUE)   if (inherits(score, "error")) {     return(failed_run(run_dir, par, par_model, res, conditionMessage(score)))   }    # 5. results   saveRDS(     list(par = par, par_model = par_model, score = score, failed = FALSE),     file.path(run_dir, "parameters.rds")   )   unlink(setdiff(     list.files(run_dir, full.names = TRUE),     file.path(run_dir, c("time_series.rds", "parameters.rds"))   ), recursive = TRUE)   score } failed_run <- function(run_dir, par, par_model, res, reason) {   saveRDS(     list(par = par, par_model = par_model, score = 1e8, failed = TRUE,       reason = reason),     file.path(run_dir, "parameters.rds")   )   writeLines(     c(reason, utils::tail(strsplit(res$stderr, "\n")[[1]], 100)),     file.path(run_dir, "failure_log.txt")   )   1e8 }
